stories.title: Dolce & Gabbana Signs Full-Floor Lease for NYC Headquarters
stories.excerpt: Luxury Italian fashion house Dolce & Gabbana has signed a long-term, 21,000-square-foot office lease at the Feil Organization’s 551 Fifth Ave. for its New York headquarters, occupying the entire ninth floor. The transaction builds on Feil’s ongoing repositioning strategy and leasing momentum at the Midtown property, which has seen more than 200,000 square feet of new transactions, including the National Women’s Soccer League. “Our vision for 551 Fifth Ave. has been focused on creating workspaces that appeal to a broad range of leading companies,” said Andrew Wiener, head of commercial leasing at The Feil Organization. “Welcoming Dolce & Gabbana, following the National Women’s Soccer League, reflects how the building continues to evolve and attract a dynamic mix of tenants looking for a premier Midtown location.” Feil was represented by Wiener, Tim Parlante and Kevin Driscoll. Dolce & Gabbana was represented by Louis D’Avanzo, Owen Koorbusch and John Fitzsimons of Cushman & Wakefield. The post Dolce & Gabbana Signs Full-Floor Lease for NYC Headquarters appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dolce & Gabbana leases 21,000 SF full floor at 551 Fifth Ave, Midtown Manhattan.
Feil Organization reports 200,000+ SF of new leasing momentum at repositioned property.
Building now anchors luxury fashion, sports (NWSL), signaling Midtown office recovery traction.
stories.summary: Dolce & Gabbana signed a long-term lease for the entire 9th floor (21,000 SF) at 551 Fifth Avenue in Midtown, following the National Women's Soccer League's earlier commitment. Feil Organization's repositioning strategy has generated over 200,000 SF of new transactions at the property. The deal reflects renewed corporate appetite for premier Midtown office space and a diversifying tenant base.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Office leasing momentum signals Midtown demand recovery, which may support nearby multifamily rents through employment growth, but this is a secondary effect in a submarket (Midtown office) already capital-constrained by conversion headwinds.

stories.title: William Warren Adds Nine Properties to Self-Storage Income Fund
stories.excerpt: William Warren Group (WWG), parent company of StorQuest Self Storage, said Wednesday the William Warren Group Self Storage Income Fund, L.P. has closed a $110.9-million contribution of nine operating StorQuest Self Storage facilities. The transaction more than doubles the fund, growing it from eight to 17 assets and to $196 million in gross asset value. The contributed properties add roughly 410,000 rentable square feet in high-barrier West Coast and Sunbelt markets, including San Rafael, Oakland, West Los Angeles, West Sacramento, Bakersfield and Palm Springs; Sun City, AZ; Reno, NV; and Hilo, HI. The fund now spans six states, with more than 845,000 rentable square feet and 9,100 units. Investors in the contributed properties rolled approximately 80% of their equity into fund units through a tax-deferred Section 721 exchange. The transaction was financed in part by a new $200-million credit facility from Wells Fargo. “This fund contribution reflects the strength of our strategy, our operating platform and the self-storage sector,” said Bill Hobin, CEO of Santa Monica-based William Warren Group. The post William Warren Adds Nine Properties to Self-Storage Income Fund appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: William Warren Self Storage Income Fund closes $110.9M contribution of nine StorQuest properties.
Fund expands from 8 to 17 assets across West Coast/Sunbelt markets; 410,000 rentable SF added.
Wells Fargo provides $200M credit facility; 80% of equity rolled tax-deferred into fund units.
stories.summary: William Warren Group's Self Storage Income Fund closed a $110.9 million contribution of nine operating StorQuest facilities, more than doubling the fund from 8 to 17 assets and $196 million in gross value. The added properties (410,000 SF) span high-barrier West Coast and Sunbelt markets including San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Reno, Phoenix, and Hawaii. Wells Fargo provided a $200 million credit facility to support the transaction, with 80% of investor equity rolled tax-deferred.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development, though signals strong capital availability and investor confidence in self-storage alternatives in premium West Coast and Sunbelt markets where multifamily is also competing for development capital and land.

stories.title: Development Site Trades within Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan
stories.excerpt: Ariel Property Advisors closed the $21-million sale of a development site at 566 Grand Ave. and 836 Dean St. in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. The corner development site comprises approximately 86,065 buildable square feet and traded for approximately $244 per buildable square foot. The transaction was arranged by Ariel partner Sean R. Kelly along with associate director Nicole Daniggelis and director Stephen Vorvolakos, who represented the seller, a long-term owner. The property was acquired by Haussmann Development, led by Josef Goodman and Jake Sokol. The site is located within the Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan, a major rezoning initiative that was approved in May 2025 with the goal of facilitating the construction of 4,600 new homes. “The Atlantic Avenue rezoning is creating a meaningful new development corridor in a part of Brooklyn that continues to see strong residential demand,” said Kelly. “The site offered the buyer significant scale, a prominent corner location and the opportunity to participate in the continued transformation of Prospect Heights and the broader Atlantic Avenue corridor.” The post Development Site Trades within Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Haussmann Development acquires $21M corner site in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn; 86,065 buildable SF.
Site trades at $244/buildable SF within Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan rezoning (approved May 2025).
Atlantic Avenue rezoning targets 4,600 new homes across Prospect Heights and broader corridor.
stories.summary: Ariel Property Advisors closed the $21 million sale of a corner development site (86,065 buildable SF) at 566 Grand Avenue and 836 Dean Street in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn to Haussmann Development. The property traded at $244 per buildable square foot. The site sits within the Atlantic Avenue Mixed-Use Plan, a major May 2025 rezoning approved to facilitate 4,600 new homes in the area.
stories.impact: Signals strong multifamily development interest in Prospect Heights as Atlantic Avenue rezoning unlocks residential density; buyer's acquisition and prominent corner positioning indicate confidence in rental demand in Brooklyn's expanding residential corridor. Zoning tailwind creates window for rapid acquisition and feasibility before land prices reflect full development potential.

stories.title: Fortune Lands Record $817M From Tyko Capital to Build Miami Faena Condo Towers
stories.excerpt: Adi Chugh’s Tyko Capital doled out Florida’s largest-ever construction loan: $817 million for the Faena-branded, waterfront condo development in Miami, the project’s sponsors announced Wednesday. Fortune International Group and Kar Properties are developing the two-tower project at 24 Southwest Fourth Street, facing the Miami River, across from Brickell City Centre. Both skyscrapers will rise 68 stories, housing 217 units each. Construction is expected to be completed in 2030. The 1.8-acre, Rafael Viñoly Architects-designed project has generated more than $500 million in sales to date, including the $30 million purchase of a penthouse, according to the sponsors. The debt transaction “demonstrates the depth of confidence in the project and the continued global appetite for best-in-class real estate in Miami,” Edgardo Defortuna, president and CEO of Fortune International Group, said in a statement. Despite interest rate hikes, lenders are still funneling mammoth construction loans for luxury condo projects in South Florida, typically after strong presales. Earlier this week, Fortune International Group, alongside Château Group, secured a $463 million loan to finish one condo tower at the St. Regis Residences condo development in Sunny Isles Beach. In 2022, Defortuna bought the Downtown Miami site for $58.8 million, partnering with KAR Properties, which had owned it since 2013, according to property records. In 2015, New York-based KAR Properties had launched sales for a luxury condo project, but construction never started. The land, which is surrounded by three condo buildings inside a gated community, stayed vacant. In 2023, Bank OZK supplied a $38 million loan for marketing costs and site work for the Faena Residences, which marks the first condo development for the hotel brand, founded by Alan Faena and billionaire Len Blavatnik in 2000. It operates an oceanfront hotel and nearby cultural event spaces in Miami Beach as well as hotels in New York and Buenos Aires. T
bullets: Tyko Capital underwrites $817M construction loan—Florida's largest ever—for Faena Miami condo towers.
Fortune/KAR Properties developing two 68-story towers (434 units total) at Miami River; $500M+ presales.
Completion targeted 2030; robust capital availability despite rate environment signals Miami luxury demand persistence.
stories.summary: Tyko Capital provided an $817 million construction loan—Florida's largest on record—for the Faena-branded waterfront condo development in Miami led by Fortune International Group and KAR Properties. The two 68-story towers will house 217 units each and are designed by Rafael Viñoly Architects. The project has already generated over $500 million in presales, with construction completion targeted for 2030.
stories.impact: Demonstrates robust capital depth and lender confidence in Miami waterfront/luxury residential, but signals capital deployment focus on high-barrier-to-entry condo projects rather than rental multifamily; may indicate tightening equity and debt availability for garden-variety rental development in Miami as premium projects crowd the capital stack.

stories.title: Fourth Sale Closes in Anaheim Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of Knott-Orange Apartments, a 35-unit multifamily property located at 515 S. Knott Ave. in Anaheim. The property sold for $9.65 million, or $275,714 per unit. “This transaction marked the fourth closing from a larger Anaheim-area multifamily portfolio as the seller continues to reposition its holdings through a 1031 exchange strategy,” said Nick Kazemi, managing director investments. “The property sold for more than 99% of the asking price, with an extended escrow period to accommodate the seller’s exchange. The buyer plans to renovate unit interiors and make property improvements to increase rental income.” Kazemi, Tyler Leeson and Matt Kipp, of Marcus & Millichap’s Orange County office, and Drew Holden, of the firm’s Las Vegas office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, a family that had owned and operated the property for more than 30 years, and procured the buyer, a Southern California-based property management company. The post Fourth Sale Closes in Anaheim Multifamily Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap closes fourth Anaheim multifamily sale: 35-unit property at $9.65M ($275,714/unit).
Seller executing 1031 exchange strategy across larger portfolio; buyer is Southern California property manager.
Property sold 99%+ asking price; buyer plans unit renovations to boost rental income.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of Knott-Orange Apartments, a 35-unit property in Anaheim, for $9.65 million ($275,714 per unit). The transaction marked the fourth closing from a larger Anaheim-area multifamily portfolio as the seller repositions holdings via 1031 exchange. The buyer, a Southern California property management company, plans interior renovations and property improvements to increase rental income.
stories.impact: Portfolio liquidation via 1031 suggests opportunistic seller timing or capital reallocation, while buyer focus on unit-level value-add indicates Anaheim rent growth fundamentals remain intact; tight pricing (99%+ of ask) and buyer profile (local operator) reflect stable, cash-flow-oriented market but limited speculative development heat in Orange County.

stories.title: JLL Arranges $135M Financing for Luxury Multifamily in Yonkers
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged $135 million in construction financing and joint venture equity for the development of The Ibex at Ridge Hill, a 282-unit luxury multifamily community at the Ridge Hill mixed-use lifestyle center in Yonkers. Senior managing directors Evan Pariser and Aaron Niedermayer and director John Lowe arranged the senior construction loan with Bank OZK and the LP equity investment from Eagle Realty Group, LLC on behalf of the development team led by Saber-Hightower and Rafferty Real Estate. Saber-Hightower acquired Parcel K at 22 Lembo Dr. in Ridge Hill earlier this month to develop a 17-story property on the site. The property will utilize an existing adjacent parking structure with 423 dedicated resident parking spaces. “Equity capital remains highly selective, particularly for ground-up development, so investors are looking closely at basis, location, product, sponsorship and their ability to execute,” said Pariser. “The Ibex checked those boxes, and we were able to structure a capital stack that positions the project well as it moves into construction.” The post JLL Arranges $135M Financing for Luxury Multifamily in Yonkers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranges $135M financing for The Ibex at Ridge Hill: 282-unit luxury multifamily in Yonkers.
Saber-Hightower/Rafferty development; Bank OZK senior loan + Eagle Realty equity stack.
17-story property; 423 dedicated parking spaces via existing adjacent structure; construction underway.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $135 million in construction financing and joint venture equity for The Ibex at Ridge Hill, a 282-unit luxury multifamily community at the Ridge Hill mixed-use center in Yonkers. Bank OZK provided the senior construction loan and Eagle Realty Group committed LP equity for the development led by Saber-Hightower and Rafferty Real Estate. The 17-story property will include 423 dedicated parking spaces.
stories.impact: Yonkers suburban-mixed-use multifamily is securing selective equity capital at scale; successful financing indicates investor confidence in suburban Westchester rental demand and the Ridge Hill ecosystem, signaling strong absorption fundamentals in the New York metro's northern suburban ring where land costs and development risk are lower than Manhattan/Brooklyn.

stories.title: Leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue Sells to Namdar Realty Group for $62M
stories.excerpt: Igal Namdar’s Namdar Realty Group has purchased the leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue for $62 million. The deal covers the entirety of the 11-story building at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 15th Street. Its Class B office and retail spaces sit at the intersection of Manhattan’s Flatiron and Union Square submarkets. The seller, a joint venture between Madison Capital and Lubert-Adler Partners, began marketing its leasehold interest in the property in 2021. Market sources at the time told Commercial Observer that the sale could net as much as $150 million. The ultimately $62 million transaction with Namdar Realty was finalized on Oct. 22, according to Traded, which first noted the sale. Meridian Capital Group’s Helen Hwang, David Schechtman, Brian Szczapa and Ian Shoenfeld facilitated the transaction. Namdar has roughly 90 years remaining on the leasehold term, according to Szczapa. Family firm Samco Properties and the family of Mark Lapidus, former global real estate chief of coworking firm WeWork, own the land underneath the property. The leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue was last acquired in 2016 by Madison Capital. The Midtown-based investment firm agreed to pay nearly $85 million upfront for the fully leased building, as well as $3.5 million in annual rent, according to The Real Deal. It is unclear when Lubert-Adler entered the arrangement. Currently, the building’s website advertises one full-floor availability spanning 15,227 square feet. Tenants there include WeWork, Dutch payment company Adyen and artificial intelligence video-editing startup Captions. An unnamed AI company recently secured a roughly 30,000-square-foot off-market lease in the building, sources fielding such hush-hush deals told CO earlier this month. The property’s ground-floor retail space is partially occupied by City National Bank, and another unit remains vacant. bullets: Namdar Realty Group acquires 71 Fifth Avenue leasehold for $62M (11-story Class B office/retail).
Property sits at Flatiron/Union Square submarket intersection; leasehold has ~90 years remaining term.
Original 2021 marketing expectation was ~$150M; transaction represents 59% markdown from initial ask.
stories.summary: Namdar Realty Group purchased the leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue, a Class B office and retail building at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 15th Street, for $62 million. The property spans all 11 stories and sits at the intersection of Manhattan's Flatiron and Union Square submarkets. The leasehold carries approximately 90 years remaining on its term; the seller (Madison Capital/Lubert-Adler JV) began marketing the asset in 2021 at much higher expectations (~$150M).
stories.impact: Office leasehold acquisition at steep discount signals Manhattan office distress and leasehold risk; limited direct multifamily relevance, though the 59% markdown from 2021 ask reflects subdued office investment demand and potential headwinds for Upper Fifth Avenue commercial-to-residential conversion economics in the near term.

stories.title: Podcast: How Yardi Is Becoming a System of Intelligence, with CEO Rob Teel
stories.excerpt: Rob Teel is the CEO of Yardi, the property management and real estate investment software company founded in 1984 whose platform serves owners and operators of commercial and residential space worldwide. He joined Yardi in 2003 and spent more than two decades leading its Global Solutions business, overseeing product direction, services, and client relationships across investment management, international, and commercial property owners before being appointed CEO in January 2026. Before Yardi, he was a consulting manager at Accenture focused on ERP and business process outsourcing, where he managed multinational systems implementations for Fortune 100 organizations. Rob is based in Santa Barbara. stories.title: Children’s Rescue Fund Adds 9K SF at the Bronx’s 521 Bergen Avenue
stories.excerpt: Nonprofit housing and supportive family services provider Children’s Rescue Fund has upped its footprint at 521 Bergen Avenue. The charity’s executive offices expanded by 8,648 square feet on the South Bronx office property’s second floor in early October, according to an announcement by landlord brokerage JLL. The deal gives Children’s Rescue Fund a total footprint of 26,646 square feet and completes the lease-up of the redeveloped building, all six stories of which are entirely occupied by nonprofits. “Having a space that is accessible, flexible and well suited to our needs allows us to strengthen our operations and remain focused on delivering the critical services that families depend on,” Children’s Rescue Fund CEO Orlando Ivey said in a statement. The building owner is 521 Bergen Properties, and the building is managed by an affiliate of Rubenstein Partners. The landlord was represented by JLL’s William Korchak, Al Gutierrez, Edward DiTolla and Henry Warner in the expansion deal. It was not immediately clear whether the tenant worked with an outside brokerage. “Completing the lease-up of 521 Bergen Avenue is a significant milestone for the property and a testament to the vision behind its redevelopment,” Korchak said in a statement. Children’s Rescue Fund arrived at 521 Bergen Avenue in November 2025. Its initial lease spanned 18,000 square feet across the third and fourth floors, as well as a portion of the basement, Commercial Observer reported at the time. That deal carried a 10-year term with an asking rent of $39 per square foot, and the same terms applied to its recent expansion. The 55,000-square-foot building, located one block from the Third Avenue–149th Street subway station, also hosts child welfare organization JCCA and programming provider The Bridge. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Children's Rescue Fund expands by 8,648 SF at 521 Bergen Avenue, South Bronx; total footprint now 26,646 SF.
Expansion completes full lease-up of six-story redeveloped building; all 100% occupied by nonprofits.
Building owner 521 Bergen Properties; managed by Rubenstein Partners affiliate; expansion closed early October.
stories.summary: Nonprofit housing and supportive family services provider Children's Rescue Fund expanded its footprint at 521 Bergen Avenue in the South Bronx by 8,648 SF on the second floor, bringing its total occupancy to 26,646 SF. The expansion completes the lease-up of the six-story redeveloped property, which is now entirely occupied by nonprofits. Rubenstein Partners manages the asset on behalf of 521 Bergen Properties.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance; nonprofit office absorption in South Bronx signals community investment and institutional interest in the neighborhood, but does not drive multifamily demand or rental rate signals. Full lease-up of nonprofit office may tighten flex/opportunity-cost space but does not materially affect residential supply or capital deployment.

stories.title: Blacksmith Software, Sona Technologies Lease 26K SF at Moinian’s 245 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: The Moinian Group signed two new technology firms at one of its Midtown South buildings. Blacksmith Software, which provides support services to users of coding platform GitHub, leased 14,000 square feet, the entire seventh floor, of 245 Fifth Avenue, while AI-driven human resources firm Sona Technologies took all of the 12,000-square-foot 19th floor, according to the landlord. The Moinian Group did not immediately provide asking rents or the length of the leases, but the average asking rent in Midtown South was $71.43 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to a report from Lee & Associates. “245 Fifth Avenue continues to attract a diverse mix of businesses seeking high-quality office space in one of Manhattan’s most dynamic commercial neighborhoods,” Omar Sozkesen, vice president of commercial leasing for the Moinian Group, said in a statement. “These transactions reflect strong demand in the building and the strength of its location, flexible floor plates and distinctive character.” Newmark’s Scott Klau, Erik Harris and Ben Klau represented Moinian while AI-native brokerage firm Tandem Space negotiated on behalf of Blacksmith. Evan Kleinberg and Lenny Kohlmayer of Cornelia Street Partners negotiated on behalf of Sona Technologies. Tandem Space and Cornelia Street did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 245 Fifth Avenue sits at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 28th Street, two blocks north of Madison Square Park. Other tenants in the building include WeWork, which signed a 55,000-square-foot lease in August 2025 — only its second lease deal since exiting Chapter 11 bankruptcy — as well as the Institute of Integrative Nutrition, which signed a 14,000-square-foot renewal in March 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Moinian Group leases 26,000 SF at 245 Fifth Avenue, Midtown South to two tech firms.
Blacksmith Software takes 14,000 SF (7th floor); Sona Technologies takes 12,000 SF (19th floor).
Market context: Midtown South average asking rent $71.43/SF Q3 2026; reflects tech tenant demand.
stories.summary: The Moinian Group signed two technology firms at 245 Fifth Avenue in Midtown South: Blacksmith Software (GitHub support services) leased 14,000 SF on the entire 7th floor, and Sona Technologies (AI-driven HR platform) took the full 12,000-SF 19th floor. The Moinian Group did not disclose asking rents or lease terms, but market context shows Midtown South averaging $71.43/SF in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Tech tenant demand in Midtown South office reflects ongoing employment influx and corporate growth in Manhattan's southern markets; signals sustained job creation and worker presence that supports nearby multifamily rental demand, though office market stress (conversion talk, high vacancies in other buildings) suggests multifamily upside may be capped by hybrid-work headwinds and office-to-residential conversion supply.
